result:
Workspace is clean (`public/` at 22MB is the real asset content needed for the build). Ready to submit.

**What changed this iteration**
- **Hero billboard rework** (from pixel forensics on `browse_home`/`movies`/`shows` references): the small "4K" square badge and "Genres" eyebrow are replaced with the wide **red NETFLIX wordmark badge** — the badge text was decoded letter-by-letter and confirmed as "NETFLIX". Title is now clickable (opens the detail modal), the synopsis is 2 lines, and the button row is now a **red play button with white triangle** plus the meta line (match% / year / duration / maturity) beside it — exactly the layout found in the references, including removal of the "More Info" pill which the reference doesn't have. Title scaled up to 7vw, width-validated against the reference glyph block (rendered "MICHAEL" ≈ measured width).
- **Games page** now uses a **centered brand hero**: red Netflix N icon + large "Games" wordmark on dark with a radial red glow, matching the decoded reference (centered red brand graphic + title) instead of a title billboard.
- Verified every referenced asset path resolves (no 404s), clean Vite build, `validate` 14/14 with chain 8/8.

**Still approximate (can't fully resolve without a browser)**
- The reference hero's exact title text is a large white display word; our app renders the real top-ranked title from the dataset, so text matches when the same title is ranked #1 and legitimately differs otherwise.
- The games hero's exact red glyph is rendered as the brand N icon — visually the same design language, tiny stroke differences possible.
- The two intentional non-2xx (`POST /api/my-list` → 422, `DELETE /api/my-list/1` → 404) remain by design.
